display.title: Episode 467: The Napkins and Toothpicks, Chapter 1 (Shabbos Zachor)
display.summary_short: Why everyone must hear Parshas Zachor before Purim, and a king's question about fairness answered with the parable of a son who wastes his father's gold on pointless toothpicks.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Zachor 5751. Uncle Yossi explains that the Torah itself commands everyone, young and old, to hear Parshas Zachor, read just before Purim because Haman descended from Amalek, who attacked the Jewish people on the way to Har Sinai. Soldiers of Tzivos Hashem should bring friends and relatives to shul too, because the Purim victory came through achdus, when Esther asked to gather all the Jews together. After the Hakochainik march, a girl from a Brooklyn girls' school leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time begins with a king who admires the Jewish people but asks a rabbi why Hashem warns only the Jews against idol worship. The rabbi answers with a parable: a devoted father gives his son 2,000 gold coins to start a business. At the fair the son buys a trainload of toothpicks with no points, and on his second try a trainload of needles with no eyes. What the father does next, and how it answers the king, is left for next week.
display.lesson: Hearing Parshas Zachor and standing together in achdus strengthen our trust that Hashem will defeat every Haman.
